operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are backtick-quoted in DDL; identifiers are mixed-case (Third_Party_Companies, Maintenance_Contracts, Engineer_Visits) — must preserve original case and double-quote in generated SQL.
All tables are tiny (3-20 rows); no huge-table sampling concern, but read_schema must still handle the 300k cap path.

DATETIME columns store TEXT like '2017-09-13 11:51:29' (space-separated, no T, no timezone); ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' — first element parses as int? No, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
VARCHAR(1) columns (chargeable_yn, gender) store '0'/'1' text — String fuzzer, not Bool/Bit.
VARCHAR(20) chargeable_amount stores '4','9' — String fuzzer, int-like strings get +1/-1 neighbors.
Several columns are 100% NULL (other_contract_details, other_part_details, other_fault_details, other_visit_details) — original_values all NULL, sampler drops None -> p:=1, always fresh.
High-null columns (other_staff_details 0.733, other_asset_details 0.733, other_details 0.867) have 1-2 distinct non-null values.

Junction tables Asset_Parts, Engineer_Skills, Fault_Log_Parts, Skills_Required_To_Fix have NO primary key (pk=[]) — sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).
All FKs point to existing parents with INTEGER PKs; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite PKs.

FK columns are NOT NULL (maintenance_contract_company_id, supplier_company_id, asset_id, part_id, engineer_id, skill_id, fault_log_entry_id, part_fault_id, recorded_by_staff_id) — TS may still emit NULLs from empty parents, causing insert failures.
contact_staff_id in Engineer_Visits is nullable FK (notnull=0) — TS may emit NULL, which is valid.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE constraints beyond PKs; 'unique'/'checked' line-scan will find nothing.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on all DATETIME columns: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals; contract dates cluster 2017-2018, visit dates span 1973-2010 — wide range per column.
Number fuzzer on all INTEGER PKs and FK columns: scale=4, range [-10^4,10^4], int perturbation +-1/+-2; PKs will be large random ints, not 1..N.
String fuzzer on VARCHAR columns: charset a-zA-Z 0-9(), length 0..20 (or args[0]); company_type VARCHAR(5) gets 0-5 char strings, not 'Supplier'/'Maintenance Contractor'.
String fuzzer on VARCHAR(1) gender/chargeable_yn: 0-1 char random strings, mostly not '0'/'1' — breaks equality predicates on these.
String fuzzer on fault_status VARCHAR(10): random strings, not 'Waiting'/'Fixed'/'Reported'/'Return' — breaks status filters.
Literal pool from train SQL will seed some real values (e.g. 'Fixed', 'Waiting', 'Supplier') but p=0.2 fresh-draw probability means most values are random.
FK consistency: child FK columns draw from parent's FINAL filtered PK values with replacement — junction tables get many duplicate (asset_id,part_id) pairs, which is fine (no PK).
Empty-parent case: if a parent table's PK filtering leaves 0 rows (unlikely here, sizes >=30), child FK gets NULLs -> NOT NULL insert failures -> rows skipped.
Known FN driver: random strings for company_type/gender/fault_status make WHERE col='Supplier' etc. return 0 rows, so gold and mutant both empty -> missed kill.
Known FP driver: junction tables with no PK get duplicate rows from FK sampling with replacement; COUNT(*) queries may differ spuriously between gold and neighbor.
Known FP driver: Date fuzzer range from 5 sampled originals can be narrow (e.g. contract dates all 2017-2018) — date-range predicates may behave differently than on full original.
Number fuzzer on PKs produces huge ints; joins still work but ORDER BY / LIMIT queries may pick different rows than original distribution.
